title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Work IQ API access to declarative agents
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, permissions, consumption licensing and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the spending-policy navigation, name the update operation's deciding properties, and remove checklist instructions for controls not represented in the table.

claims.claim: Work IQ API use is admin-opt-in through admin-approved permissions and configured usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API. Register a client application and grant the delegated WorkIQAgent.Ask permission.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages give no fixed credit rate for requests to declarative agents as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ declarative agent requests Copilot Credits fixed rate Chat Context pricing. Opened Work IQ overview, API overview, retrieve, cost-considerations and billing overview; none gives a fixed per-request declarative-agent rate.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's pricing announcement describes Work IQ Chat and Context consumption as variable.
claims.quote: Variable | Work IQ Chat API or Work IQ Context API | Variable (Scenarios Below)

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals provisions the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals.

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI setting for the one-time Work IQ service-principal provisioning is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ enable service principal admin center UI tenant default automatic first use admin consent. Opened enable-work-iq, permissions and MCP overview; provisioning is through Graph Explorer or Azure CLI, not an admin-centre setting.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Global Administrator performs the one-time Work IQ setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: The provisioning operation is one-time per organisation.
claims.quote: one-time per organization. This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization

claims.claim: The provisioning request body sets appId to the Work IQ application ID.
The enablement page also documents an Azure CLI provisioning route.
claims.quote: az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7

claims.claim: Admin consent is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: select Entra ID, and then select App registrations. Select API permissions ... Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].

claims.claim: az ad app permission admin-consent --id <APP_ID> grants consent for the app's configured permissions.
claims.quote: Add the WorkIQAgent.Ask delegated permission and grant consent. az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: WorkIQAgent.Ask is a delegated permission.
claims.quote: WorkIQAgent.Ask ... Delegated ... Ask Work IQ agents on behalf of the user

claims.claim: WorkIQAgent.Ask requires admin consent, providing an app-level gate for calls.
claims.quote: WorkIQAgent.Ask ... AdminConsentRequired ... Yes

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].note; Governance controls: spending row
claims.claim: Copilot > Cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center is the spending-policy dashboard entry point.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with ... Work IQ API.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits#edit-spending-policy to sources; it documents selecting Configuration and the policy, then editing Billing method and Spending limits in the details fly-out.

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls: spending row
claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates an existing spending policy's limits and billing methods.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods. PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[2].note and its rendered counterpart: 'The request body uses periodLimit and perUserLimit for limits, and billingMethods for funding. Adding payAsYouGo to stored non-pay-as-you-go funding also requires a complete billingInstrument.' These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-update.

claims.claim: The spending-policy update API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Spending policies can govern selected groups.
claims.quote: Apply limits to selected security groups | selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy

claims.claim: Group assignments and service settings use separate operations rather than the spending-policy update operation.
claims.quote: Read serviceSettings, emailThresholdSettings, and group assignments through their own endpoints; these relationships aren't expandable.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API operation to configure Work IQ MCP tenant policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy API Graph copilot admin settings update Work IQ policy; "Work IQ" "policy" "PATCH". Opened policy-governance-mcp, MCP overview and permissions; found no policy-setting HTTP operation or cmdlet.

claims.claim: The initial MCP policy control is tenant-level rather than per-user, per-app or per-agent.
claims.quote: Tenant-level control applies across the tenant. Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The Policy tab, when available, lets admins review policy state and turn tenant policy on or off.
claims.quote: select the Policy tab when it's available. Review the current policy state, then turn policy on or off for the tenant as needed.

claims.claim: Declarative agents configure instructions, knowledge and actions instead of a custom conversational runtime.
claims.quote: You configure the agent's instructions, knowledge sources, and supported capabilities rather than implementing and hosting your own conversational runtime.

claims.claim: Work IQ endpoints include A2A, remote MCP and REST.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Retrieval uses the built-in Microsoft 365 Copilot agent by default.
claims.quote: By default, retrieval uses the built-in Microsoft 365 Copilot agent.

claims.claim: A retrieve caller can pass an available declarative agent's identifier in agentId.
claims.quote: To retrieve through another available declarative agent, pass its identifier in agentId.

claims.claim: The retrieve tool is public preview.
claims.quote: The retrieve tool is available in public preview.

claims.claim: The A2A quickstart supports choosing a specific agent by its agent ID.
claims.quote: To invoke a specific agent, pass its agent ID through --agent-id.

claims.claim: Some Word, Excel and PowerPoint agents do not produce useful headless A2A responses.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 agents (notably Word, Excel, and PowerPoint agents in the Copilot Chat UI) are designed to run in the context of those Office products and don't produce useful responses when invoked headlessly via A2A.

claims.claim: A nondefault agentId must not be combined with a nonempty capabilities array.
claims.quote: Don't combine a nondefault agentId with a nonempty capabilities array.

claims.quote: The declarative agent defines its own data scope

claims.claim: Work IQ rejects requests that add a separate capability scope to a nondefault declarative agent.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ requests run in the signed-in user's context.
claims.quote: Requests run in the context of the signed-in user.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: WorkIQAgent.Ask covers read and write access to Microsoft 365 resources accessible to Work IQ agents and scoped to the user.

claims.claim: No source states that Work IQ API use is on for the tenant without admin consent and billing setup.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ enable service principal admin center UI tenant default automatic first use admin consent. Opened enable-work-iq, permissions, MCP overview and retrieve; automatic principal creation is documented, but consent and billing remain prerequisites.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Calling users must have a spending policy that includes Work IQ API to consume its credits.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Work IQ retrieval and chat do not grant access beyond the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: Retrieve returns source content with sensitivity-label metadata when available.
claims.quote: sensitivityLabel | object | Sensitivity-label metadata for the source, when available.

claims.claim: Microsoft tells the caller not to treat missing or unrecognised contentProtection as an allow decision.
claims.quote: Don't treat a missing, failed, blocked, or unrecognized value as an allow decision.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra delegated authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP mutation operations are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported MCP mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The MCP policy's applicability to A2A and REST calls targeting declarative agents is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy settings Microsoft Graph API update policy A2A REST declarative agents restrict agent access. Opened policy-governance-mcp and API overview; policy can apply across experiences, but no passage confirms these specific calls.

claims.claim: Retrieve tool schemas can evolve.
claims.quote: Tool availability and schemas can evolve, so use the schema returned by tools/list as the source of truth instead of hard-coding a locally copied schema.

claims.claim: A 403 can result from the user not belonging to a usage-based billing plan.
claims.quote: 403 Forbidden (no scope error) | User not a member of a usage-based billing plan.

claims.claim: A 403 can result from missing WorkIQAgent.Ask admin consent.
claims.quote: 403 Forbidden with Required scopes = [...] | Admin consent for WorkIQAgent.Ask wasn't granted.

claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence are billed based on usage.
claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.claim: For licensed users Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence does not replenish the Work IQ API credit balance.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license doesn't replenish the Work IQ API credit balance.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses a Copilot Credit pool shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: The Work IQ setup page requires a usage-based billing plan with an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: Spending policies govern access and spending limits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go can allow usage to continue after prepaid credits run out.
claims.quote: Configure an Azure subscription as a billing method so usage can continue when prepaid credits run out. ... Spending limits still apply.

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one spending policy does not exclude it from other policies.
claims.quote: Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says the service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time. In some corner cases ... the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting specifically limiting which declarative agents the Work IQ endpoint can reach.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ declarative agents admin restrict block available agents endpoint agentId access management; "Work IQ" "declarative" "block". Read retrieve, A2A, MCP policy and agent-actions excerpt; general agent blocking is not stated to govern Work IQ endpoint agent selection.

claims.claim: Cost management can report consumption by user and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab enables detailed analysis by spending policy, user, group, agent, or service.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist's service-selection and user-assignment controls have corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: "whether Work IQ API is selected"; "Assign pilot users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API." Table: "user/group assignments and service access use separate operations." The spending row covers limits and billing methods.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Assign pilot users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.' Replace the Before rollout spending-policy bullet with 'Review the spending policies that would cover those users, including their per-user and policy limits and billing method.' These controls have no row; do not add rows in this correction.

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft tells developers to discover retrieve schemas with tools/list rather than hard-code a copied schema.

claims.claim: The Work IQ setup page requires a resource group assigned to the billing plan.

claims.claim: Spending policies do not reserve credits.

claims.claim: Manual service-principal provisioning is needed in some corner cases, such as configuring MCP policy before first use.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the Work IQ policy layer can apply across Work IQ experiences.
claims.quote: This policy layer can apply across Work IQ experiences. This article focuses on how policy governance applies to Work IQ MCP tool requests.

claims.claim: The permissions documentation requires an administrator to enable Work IQ before applications use its permissions.
claims.quote: An organization administrator must enable Work IQ in your organization before these permissions can be used by applications.

claims.claim: The calling application needs a Microsoft Entra registration.
claims.quote: Register an application with permissions to access Work IQ.

claims.claim: Work IQ requests can fail with quota errors that repeated retries do not resolve.
claims.quote: A Work IQ chat request can fail with QuotaExhausted ... Repeated retries won't resolve a depleted balance or an exhausted spending limit.
